result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as test code, whatever follows it. The new test passes (2 tests, 0 failures).

**What changed**

- `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (around lines 393–394): the two mock rules used `[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+`, which required at least one character after `mock` and rejected punctuation and non-ASCII. They now read `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*` and `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`. `[^/]*` keeps the match inside one folder name, and `pathMatches` already normalizes backslashes, so Windows paths are covered.
- `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java` (new): checks the real test-convention list against the cases in the task. The positive cases include the plain `mock/` folder, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe`, `mock模拟` and backslash paths, plus the existing `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/`. The negative cases are `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java` and `mockery.java`.

I did not touch the existing `[Mm]ocks/` rule, and I did not commit. I added the test file because it was the only way I could check the patterns here: the sandbox blocked a scratch file in `/tmp`.
